pages_convention: PDF pages counted from 1 (identical to the printed 'n of 17' page labels)

entry.evidence: the dynamics of S at intra-annual time scales (e.g., aggregated precipitation events or monthly aggregates) remain poorly understood in many hydroclimates

steps.action: Posed the gap: whether intra-annual storage-driven precipitation partitioning differs between water- and energy-limited catchments, especially those near the P/PET = 1 threshold.
steps.quote: To address this knowledge gap, we used measured and calculated daily parameters of the water budget

steps.action: Selected two threshold catchments (Calhoun, Tilden) and two strongly energy-limited catchments (Lower Hafren, Luquillo), and matched a Normal and a Wet water year at each site by precipitation percentile.
steps.quote: to capture similar precipitation percentiles across all four study catchments

steps.action: Assembled daily P and Q for Calhoun from the authors' own tipping-bucket gauge and v-notch weir stage records.
steps.quote: We employed daily data collected by the authors from Calhoun and Tilden and publicly available hydroclimatic data

steps.action: Reused the Tilden water-balance data (P plus golf-course irrigation, rating-curve Q, satellite AET) from the authors' earlier publication.
steps.quote: Tilden's data was published in Grande et al. (2020).

steps.action: Took Lower Hafren and Luquillo daily P, Q and meteorological data from public datasets used by other groups (Harman 2015; Silver & Leon 2019; Zimmerman 2018).
steps.quote: The data used from Lower Hafren was previously used by (Harman, 2015)

steps.action: Estimated daily ET (Thornthwaite PET with AET assumed equal to PET at energy-limited sites; Penman-Monteith scaled ET at Lower Hafren) and integrated P - Q - ET from 1 October to obtain daily relative catchment storage.
steps.quote: Relative storage (mm) for each day (t) was estimated as:

steps.action: Defined precipitation events with an inclusive P-and-Q rule (onset of P >= 1 mm/d to recession to 120% of pre-event Q), yielding 301 events.
steps.quote: Here, we defined precipitation events from the onset of P ≥ 1 mm/day

steps.action: Computed event runoff ratios from baseflow-separated event flow (recession-analysis algorithm, EcoHydRology R package) and normalized event values by event length.
steps.quote: We calculated event-flow using a baseflow separation algorithm based on recession analysis

steps.action: Reported annual water budgets per site and year, including Tilden switching from water-limited (Normal year) to energy-limited (Wet year).
steps.quote: Moreover, we found a shift between water-limited in the normal water year and energy-limited in the wet water year at Tilden

steps.action: Described event-scale P, ET, Q and RR statistics and their seasonal partitioning to storage, runoff and ET at each catchment.
steps.quote: These variations in P partitioning were seasonal, with the largest partitioning to S at the beginning of the water year

steps.action: Established a pattern in storage common across water years and sites and named three storage stages: wet-up, plateau and dry-down.
steps.quote: Based on this common pattern in S across water years and sites, we categorized S seasonality into three different stages

steps.action: Compared runoff ratio against antecedent storage and found clockwise hysteresis in both threshold catchments, wide at Tilden and narrow and tall at Calhoun.
steps.quote: the S-RR relationship revealed hysteretic behaviour with a clockwise direction across each water year

steps.action: Contrasted the threshold catchments with the strongly energy-limited reference catchments, where no S-RR hysteresis appeared and storage stayed high.
steps.quote: In contrast, hysteretic behaviour was not observed in the S-RR relationship for the strongly energy-limited watersheds

steps.action: Proposed a conceptual model of storage stages controlling partitioning (wet-up fills storage, plateau routes P to Q, dry-down routes P to ET), offered as hypotheses for future testing.
steps.quote: Here, we present a conceptual model that characterizes differences and similarities in storage-driven hydrologic partitioning

steps.action: Compared the stage model with published storage-threshold (fill-and-spill) work and with the S-Q periods of Fovet et al. (2015) and Spence et al. (2010), finding consistency.
steps.quote: The P, Q and S dynamics observed during the plateau confirm this previous knowledge

steps.action: Hypothesized that ET redistributes dry-down precipitation into indirect, plant-accessible storage (after Dralle et al. 2018), explaining the hysteresis; not tested here.
steps.quote: We hypothesize redistribution of the incoming P during the dry-down stage into less hydraulically active but more plant-accessible storage zones

steps.action: Defended the stage identification against uncertain ET by arguing that uniformly distributed ET errors shift storage magnitude but not curve shape; no check was performed.
steps.quote: uncertainties in the magnitude of ET, as long as the errors are uniformly distributed, should result in similar S shapes

steps.action: Kept the claim that the storage stages and the intra-annual shifts in runoff generation are characteristic of catchments near the water/energy threshold.
steps.quote: suggests a characteristic behaviour of catchments close to this threshold.

tree.answer: Nature repeats: two years at each of two threshold catchments
Pattern recurs across both years and both threshold sites; absent in energy-limited references
Kept as a conceptual model and hypotheses for future testing

end.claim: In catchments near the water/energy-limitation threshold, storage passes through wet-up, plateau and dry-down stages that control event runoff ratios and produce clockwise S-RR hysteresis; this behaviour is absent in strongly energy-limited catchments and is stated to hold where saturation-excess runoff dominates.

decisive_move.sentence: Integrating the daily water balance into relative catchment storage is what makes the storage stages and the S-RR hysteresis visible; without it there is no claim.

gates.evidence: The authors chose catchments 'we expected to have the highest dependence on storage for runoff generation' (p. 9), but data availability fixed the years (p. 12-13), and no hypothesis was stated before acquisition. The pattern could have failed to recur at Tilden or in the second year, and the energy-limited sites act as references, but no formal test or threshold was set. Nothing was pre-registered; event and stage definitions were set by the authors without a stated prior fixing.

imports.item: hysteresis loops to describe storage-discharge and storage-runoff ratio relations
CalETa satellite-based daily AET mapping (Formation Environmental)

novelty_claims.quote: We believe our work can serve as a first assessment for periods in which managed aquifer recharge should not be performed
The conceptual model of storage stages in the present study thus advances ideas proposed by Fovet et al. (2015) and Spence et al. (2010)

limits: Only two water years per site are analysed (p. 12-13), so the regularity rests on few repetitions. No uncertainty is propagated into relative storage or runoff ratios, and the ET-uncertainty defence is an argument, not a check. No formal statistical test of the hysteresis or of differences between stages is reported. Sub-claims: the stage-based conceptual model is a best_explanation without stated rivals; the ET redistribution to indirect storage (p. 12) is a hypothesis with status none; the claim that findings are 'transferable across several regions' (p. 10) is unsupported beyond four catchments. The acknowledgements mention an editor and two referees, but no review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. Inference from the text: there are internal inconsistencies, for example section 3.2 labels Calhoun 2015 as wet and 2016 as normal, and Tilden 2018 as wet and 2017 as normal, the reverse of Table 1; and Tilden wet-year ET is given as 782 mm on p. 6 but 1049 mm in Table 1. These suggest the reporting was not cross-checked. Event-delineation and baseflow-separation choices were not varied, so the sensitivity of the runoff ratios to them is unknown.

disagreements.target: Long-term annual water balance / Budyko classification of catchments as water- or energy-limited
disagreements.support: Event and monthly storage analysis shows threshold catchments switching between water- and energy-limited behaviour within a year, which annual averages mask.
disagreements.quote: annual water balance studies may ‘miss’ the intra-annual variability in runoff generation

disagreements.target: Fovet et al. (2015) characterization of S-Q periods
disagreements.support: The paper's stage model gives ET a central role in the dry-down hysteresis, which Fovet et al. omitted.
disagreements.quote: Interestingly, Fovet et al. (2015) did not consider the role of ET in their characterization of the different periods.

disagreements.target: Previous studies using storage proxies (antecedent precipitation indices, water table measurements)
disagreements.support: The paper uses a water-balance estimate of integrated storage instead of proxies, and acknowledges an uncertainty tradeoff.
disagreements.quote: Previous studies have used other proxies for storage, such as antecedent precipitation indices, or water table measurements.

alternatives_considered.chosen: Inclusive event definition using both P and Q (onset of P >= 1 mm/d to Q recession to 120% of pre-event level)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: P-only definitions (Singh et al. 2018; Rinderer et al. 2016); Q threshold; groundwater-change threshold; baseflow-separation-based delineation; start of P to end of quickflow (Detty & McGuire 2010); McCarter et al. 2020 approach
alternatives_considered.reason: Precipitation regimes vary across catchments and the approach must extract periods across the entire water year for comparison

alternatives_considered.chosen: Recession-analysis baseflow separation (Sujono et al. 2004) on daily streamflow
alternatives_considered.reason: Simplicity, wide use, and successful prior use on daily streamflow series

alternatives_considered.chosen: Direct water-balance estimate of integrated storage
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Storage proxies such as antecedent precipitation indices or water table measurements
alternatives_considered.reason: Direct estimation of integrated storage, accepting greater uncertainty

alternatives_considered.chosen: Two water years at Lower Hafren and Luquillo matched by precipitation percentile to the Calhoun and Tilden years
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Longer available records at Lower Hafren and Luquillo
alternatives_considered.reason: To capture similar precipitation percentiles across all four catchments, given the short records at the main sites

alternatives_considered.chosen: Tilden irrigation combined with P as a single input
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Treating irrigation as a separate water-budget component
alternatives_considered.reason: Irrigation is applied to a small area and is less than 3% of P over the study period
